author: Elastic
attributes.description: Detects three or more Vertex AI GenerateContent replies in 60 minutes whose assistant text indicates a refusal (cannot fulfill/assist/help/answer, unable to assist, decline the request, against my guidelines, and similar), aggregated by project and model. Prompt-response logs lack a stable caller identity, so this is a project-wide refusal burst signal — pivot to auditlogs for principal/IP attribution.
false_positives: Approved red-team suites that intentionally elicit refusals. Exclude those models or raise the threshold.
attributes.name: GCP Vertex AI Repeated Assistant Refusals
attributes.note:
## Triage and analysis

### Investigating GCP Vertex AI Repeated Assistant Refusals

One project/model pair produced three or more refusal-style completions in the lookback window
(assistant text such as "I cannot fulfill…", "I cannot provide…", "unable to assist…", or
"against my guidelines…", typically with `finish_reason` STOP). Aggregation is project-wide
because prompt_response_logs do not carry caller email/IP; use auditlogs to attribute the burst.

#### Possible investigation steps

- Review `Esql.event_count`, `Esql.prompt_values`, and `Esql.response_values` on the alert. Skim
  prompts for jailbreak attempts, malware requests, or credential harvesting.
- Remember this rule keys on textual refusals with STOP — not provider `SAFETY` blocks. Use the
  safety-filter / elevated-rating rules for those.
- Pivot to `logs-gcp_vertexai.auditlogs-*` with `event.action like "*GenerateContent*"` in the same
  window for `source.ip` and `client.user.email`.
- Correlate with jailbreak-heuristic, elevated-safety, and BLOCK_NONE alerts for the same
  project/model.

### False positive analysis

- Quoted refusal examples and non-security limitations can also match these text heuristics. Read
  the original prompts and responses before treating a match as a policy refusal.
- Approved content-safety evaluation or red-team suites that intentionally elicit refusals. Exclude
  those models/principals or raise the count threshold.

### Response and remediation

- Identify the calling workload via auditlogs; if unauthorized, restrict or rotate credentials and
  review application allowlists.
- If prompts show a clear attack theme, expand the hunt across other models and projects for the
  same principal/IP.
attributes.query:
from logs-gcp_vertexai.prompt_response_logs-*
| where
    data_stream.dataset == "gcp_vertexai.prompt_response_logs" and
    MV_CONTAINS(gcp.vertexai.prompt_response_logs.full_response.candidates.finish_reason, "STOP")
| eval response_text = to_lower(coalesce(mv_concat(gcp.vertexai.prompt_response_logs.full_response.candidates.content.parts.text, " "), ""))
| where
    response_text like "*cannot fulfill*" or
    response_text like "*cannot assist*" or
    response_text like "*can't assist*" or
    response_text like "*can't help*" or
    response_text like "*cannot help*" or
    response_text like "*i cannot provide*" or
    response_text like "*i can't provide*" or
    response_text like "*i will not provide*" or
    response_text like "*i cannot answer*" or
    response_text like "*i can't answer*" or
    response_text like "*unable to provide*" or
    response_text like "*unable to assist*" or
    response_text like "*unable to fulfill*" or
    response_text like "*not able to help*" or
    response_text like "*not able to provide*" or
    response_text like "*must decline*" or
    response_text like "*respectfully decline*" or
    response_text like "*decline this request*" or
    response_text like "*decline that request*" or
    response_text like "*cannot disclose*" or
    response_text like "*can't disclose*" or
    response_text like "*against my guidelines*" or
    response_text like "*that violates my guidelines*"
| stats
    Esql.event_count = count(*),
    Esql.timestamp_first_seen = min(@timestamp),
    Esql.timestamp_last_seen = max(@timestamp),
    Esql.prompt_values = values(gcp.vertexai.prompt_response_logs.full_request.contents.parts.text),
    Esql.response_values = values(gcp.vertexai.prompt_response_logs.full_response.candidates.content.parts.text)
  by
    gcp.vertexai.prompt_response_logs.model,
    cloud.project.id
| where Esql.event_count >= 3
| keep
    gcp.vertexai.prompt_response_logs.model,
    cloud.project.id,
    Esql.event_count,
    Esql.timestamp_first_seen,
    Esql.timestamp_last_seen,
    Esql.prompt_values,
    Esql.response_values
attributes.setup:
## Setup

Requires GCP Vertex AI `prompt_response_logs` with response text populated in BigQuery export.
